overview: Two quantities people mix up constantly — one is a property of the object itself, the other depends on gravity.
genZNote: Your mass follows you to the Moon. Your weight does not.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: Amount of matter in an object; a measure of inertia.
aspects.valueB: The gravitational force acting on an object's mass.

aspects.label: Quantity Type
aspects.valueB: Vector (a force, acting toward the center of the gravitating body).

aspects.label: SI Unit
aspects.valueB: Newton (N) — it is a force, not a mass unit.

aspects.label: Changes With Location?
aspects.valueA: No — mass is constant regardless of location.
aspects.valueB: Yes — weight changes with local gravitational field strength (e.g. less on the Moon).
